database_open_paths.detail: appDatabaseProvider awaits AppDatabase.open(); production resolves documents/pandapay.sqlite and calls openFile(). AppDatabase._ opens raw sqlite3, sets WAL/busy_timeout, creates schema and runs schema migrations. This is the actual normal app database path.

SMS listener independently calls AppDatabase.open(), captures into SmsImportStore, then closes the connection. On main DB open/write failure during recovery it persists raw sender/body/timestamp into separate pandapay-recovery-deferred-sms.sqlite and later drains into normal intake.
SmsCaptureWorker spawns an isolate with database path; worker opens an independent AppDatabase.openFile() connection and captures batched messages through FinancialStore/SmsImportStore.

withRecoveryDatabase sets ordinary same-path connections query_only, opens separate SQLite handle and BEGIN IMMEDIATE; callers are required to drain sync, SMS, receipt operations first. This is still raw sqlite3, with no encrypted open in the path.

writer_reader_inventory.area: SMS ingress, intake, observations and reconciliation
writer_reader_inventory.writers_readers: OS listener writes financial SMS through SmsImportStore; bulk capture isolate writes batches; foreground inbox scanner persists provider checkpoints only after capture; recovery deferred spool preserves intake when DB is fenced; providers reconcile pending and legacy rows by active namespace.

SyncQueue persists namespaced edits/outbox state; SyncEngine pushes, pulls, materializes and acknowledges under AccountRecoveryOperationGate. Sync API is session-only; queue is sourced from shared AppDatabase.

Current cache namespace is signed-out when no token, user:<JWT subject> when present, else session:<SHA-256 token>. Shared install DB partitions most financial/cache rows by namespace. No current runtime guest namespace was found in this selection; secure receipt custody code defines user:/guest: labels but is not connected to the attachment repository.

TransactionAttachmentsRepository copies picked bytes/files in plaintext under documents/transaction_attachments/<transactionId>, then records path and metadata in transaction_attachments. Detail view reads with Image.file, opens external app or shares original path; delete removes DB row then file. Quick add also invokes repository add methods.

OCR helpers read source paths into memory and create temporary preprocessed image files; no attachment-key custody or encrypted receipt store call site was found in app/lib. Receipt OCR presence does not establish OCR-on-attachment integration.

Local snapshot reads a transactionally consistent namespace-filtered DB snapshot and all transaction attachment paths; collector copies attachment bytes to staging. Archive encrypts portable artifact with user passphrase. Restore stages/decrypts, then LocalPortableRestoreWriter replaces local state and writes restored attachment bytes/paths. Local attachments therefore have a separate portable encrypted backup flow; this does not encrypt live attachment files.

Coordinator is disabled by default at construction unless caller enables it; create requires explicit pending-data approval and captures via exclusive recovery lease. Restore requires explicit approval and writes fresh namespace. Recovery can include receipts by consent.

encrypted_components_vs_runtime_wiring.runtime_wiring_finding: A name-based rg search of checked-in app/lib surfaced AppDatabase production open using sqlite3.open directly and attachment repository/UI using plaintext File copy/read/share/delete. The search surfaced no direct app/lib call sites for EncryptedDatabaseCopy, LocalDatabaseKeyCustody, EncryptedReceiptFileStore, or LocalReceiptKeyCustody outside their secure_storage definitions. Treat those components as not observed on the inventoried runtime paths, rather than as proof against indirect/dynamic integrations; they are not evidence of active data-at-rest protection in the paths cited here.

gaps: Normal foreground and SMS background database connections do not use encrypted database open/migration code in their call paths.
Normal live receipt attachments are copied and consumed as plaintext files; the encrypted receipt/key components have no observed runtime call sites.
Database is shared across signed-out/account namespaces, while current namespace uses signed-out/user/session labels; secure receipt custody's guest namespace is not wired to this runtime model.
